counterfactual.change: No biomarker relaxation works: even all-comers (100%) predicts 282 months at 85 sites. The binding constraints are elsewhere — N=340 against 189 competing trials; feasibility would need ~510 sites even without the biomarker.

drivers: active disease thresholds (tender/swollen joint counts, CRP/ESR elevation) exclude many MTX-IR patients who are only mildly active
prior biologic/TNF exposure and non-response exclusions remove a substantial fraction of inadequate-responders
stable background therapy requirements (DMARD/steroid dose stability for 4-12 weeks) and steroid dose caps (≤10mg/day) exclude unstable or higher-dose patients
general eligibility restrictions (age limits, exclusion of other rheumatic disease, recent major surgery, active infection) remove additional patients
eligibility.reasoning: Across precedent RA trials, activity-level thresholds (tender/swollen joints, CRP/ESR), prior biologic exposure exclusions, and stable background therapy/steroid dose requirements are recurring filters that would exclude a sizable share of seropositive MTX-IR patients even after the biomarker requirement is met. Combining these compounding filters (each retaining roughly 60-85%) yields an overall pass-rate multiplier of about 0.35.

failedPrecedents.whyStopped: Business decision based on lack of enrollment
The biological effect seen with natalizumab was not sufficient to warrant further development in RA.

why: 340 patients (effect size d=0.35) at 85 sites (p75 of at-scale precedents); precedent velocity 0.65 pt/site/mo across 196 completed trials (sampled from 2268 registered), narrowed by 60% biomarker prevalence and 35% eligibility pass rate, with ~189 interventional trials competing for the same patients.
